The Harpy, (Built 1904 as "HMS Harpy"), Tower Bridge. Time Out, Jan 2025: "London s No. 1 Best Airbnb"
The Harpy – London’s Most Iconic & Historic Houseboat
Built in 1904, HMS Harpy was the world’s first floating Customs & Excise office and The City of London's royal landing stage.
Moored just west of Tower Bridge, two significant royal events: HM King George V visited The Harpy in 1920, with the then HRH The Prince of Wales (latterly HM King Edward VIII - the one who abdicated), to thank the Customs Officers working on board for their service during the First World War.
The current HM King Charles III visited in 1979 to give The Harpy's current owner The Civic Trust Award (of which he is Patron) for the restoration & conversion of the adjoining listed Victorian warehouses at New Concordia Wharf.
(see the photos in our Gallery )
When in the Gallery, click on 'More Photos' to see all of them
The Harpy features in the Legoland London model – a true London icon!
Decommissioned in 1980, The Harpy was acquired by pioneer Docklands developer Andrew Wadsworth , relocated to the South Bank , 400m east of Tower Bridge, and transformed into a spectacular 1,850 sq ft (172 sq m) four-bedroom floating home.
The Daily Telegraph described The Harpy as “A Magical Family Home.”
Available for holiday lets/vacation rentals, The Harpy offers unbeatable views of Tower Bridge , The City , and Canary Wharf .
The Harpy sleeps up to 12 guests in 4 cabins, 3 sofa beds, and a cot - perfect for families or groups.
Nearby London landmarks: Tower Bridge, The Tower of London, St. Katherine's Dock, HMS Belfast, Southwark Cathedral and the 1,000 year old Borough Market, are within easy walking distance.
Bermondsey Station, on the Jubilee Line is 10 minutes walk, London Bridge Mainline & Underground Station; 15 minutes.
Minimum stay : 3 nights (7 over Christmas/New Year/Easter)
Discounts : 15% off 4 weeknights or 10% off 7+ nights
Deposit : 25% to secure, with balance due 2 months before arrival

The Harpy has been meticulously restored and refitted into a one-off London home - original features with modern comfort and style.
The Sunday Times Travel Magazine described The Harpy as:
“So carefully restored she feels as much museum as home-from-home.”
1920s early modernist Heal’s oak furniture, deep sofas, organic cotton mattresses, Egyptian linen, and luxurious bathrooms. The fully equipped kitchen and bold, eclectic décor include oak floors, Turkish kilims, tribal fabrics, and curated art and objects. Smart touches include dimmable LED lighting, super-fast fibre optic WiFi, Sky Q TV, a 55” curved QLED TV, and an 8-speaker Sonos/Bose system.
Spacious decks and the unrivalled postcard view of Tower Bridge complete the unique and memorable experience.
From 2015, when first available for holiday lets/vacation rentals, guests have consistently given The Harpy 5 star reviews - on this website, Facebook, Google, and Airbnb – with many distinguished guests returning time and again.
